evidence.claim: The detector cannot produce a clip-edge artefact. predict_unet_transformer.py uses windows of 2 frames with stride 1 and no padding: frame 0 is detected in slot 0 of [0,1] and every other frame in slot 1 of [t-1,t]. TemporalUNet3D mixes time only through per-voxel multi-head attention with no temporal positional encoding, so it treats both slots the same way. Frame 99 goes through the same function as frame 50. Hypothesis part (a), the padding, does not exist.
evidence.source: tools/repo/scripts/predict_unet_transformer.py L348-403; tools/repo/src/biohub_tracking/models/temporal_unet.py L30-48 and L119-140 (the exp39 notebook patches this script with count==1 replacements and keeps the loop)

evidence.claim: The clip-edge excess is real. FN rate per GT edge slot: 7.8 / 8.1 / 8.1% for the first three slots, 6.0 / 6.3 / 9.0% for the last three, and 5.1% in the middle. Both embryos show it. The excess comes from a_never (40.7 per 1000 at s0 vs 13.9 mid) and a_tail (28.5 vs 3.8 mid); swaps are LOWER at the edges. The total excess over the middle-frame rate is about 154 FN edges (a_tail ~111, a_never ~118, other classes below mid).
evidence.source: own computation: .public_local_cache/l2_fn_anatomy/fn_exp39.parquet + TP edges of .public_local_cache/l2_edge_anatomy/edges_exp39.parquet (199 videos, T=100)

evidence.claim: The ILP-selected node set has a 3-frame density ramp at both ends. Real nodes per frame relative to the clip mean: t0 0.928, t1 0.976, t2 1.030, then a plateau of ~1.085 over t3-10; t94-96 ~0.925, then t97 0.881, t98 0.837, t99 0.789. This is about 15% / 10% / 5% below trend at each end, roughly 12.6k missing nodes in total (~0.6%). Gap-closing synthetic nodes also vanish at the ends: 0, 9, 27 at t0-2 and 4, 4, 0 at t97-99, vs 275 per frame mid (summed over 199 videos).
evidence.source: own computation on friend A cache raw/<stem>.geff (ILP solution, solution flag = 1 for every stored node) and ckpt/<stem>.npz

evidence.claim: Root cause: the ILP cost set. The exp39 notebook uses ILP appearance 0.0, disappearance 2, edge weight -1*p, division 1.0. tracksdata ILPSolver forces disappear == node for every node without out-edges and applies the same weight at every t, with no exemption for the last frame. A track is selected only if its summed edge probability exceeds 2, i.e. it needs at least 3 edges. So a segment that starts at t >= 97 can never be selected, and a segment that ends at t <= 2 pays the full cost even though its earlier part lies before the clip.

Measured confirmation in the ILP solution. The track-start fraction is 5.3% per frame mid-clip and exactly 0 at t = 97, 98, 99. The track-end fraction is 5.4% mid and exactly 0 at t = 0, 1, 2. Mid-clip, 15.8% of nodes sit in segments aged <= 2 frames, vs 10.5 / 5.4 / 0% at t97 / 98 / 99. The mirror measure (remaining <= 2) is 16.1% mid vs 0 / 5 / 9.8% at t0 / 1 / 2. This matches the density ramp.

Ultrack (Royer lab, same group as the organisers and tracksdata) removes exactly this artefact: appear_weight = not(is_first_t | is_border) * appear_weight and disappear_weight = not(is_last_t | is_border) * disappear_weight. tracksdata's ILPSolver does not do this automatically.
Motile documents the same trade-off: a high appear cost encourages continuous tracks but can lead to not selecting short tracks at all, which is the regime our d2/a0 ILP is in at the clip ends.

Part (b), the tail change, is about break-even. Short (< 6 node) pre-tail components touching t=0 with >= 4 nodes hold 66 a_tail FN edges but add 11.8k nodes. Those touching t=99 hold 55 FN edges and add 11.3k nodes. With >= 5 nodes: 41 FN / 6.5k nodes and 28 FN / 6.2k nodes. A mean edge-probability gate of 0.5 or 0.7 barely separates them. Edge gain ~60 x 7.4e-6 = +0.00045 per side vs node multiplier -0.1 x 0.93 x 0.59% = -0.00055 per side.
evidence.source: own computation: ckpt/<stem>.npz components joined to a_tail FN rows (u_near/v_near = ckpt node id) of fn_exp39.parquet, 199 videos

evidence.claim: The nodes the ILP drops at the clip ends are low-value. The ~118 excess a_never FN edges spread over ~12.6k missing nodes is ~0.009 TP edges per node, vs ~0.061 for an average final node. The node cost is ~4.6e-8 per node and the edge value ~7.4e-6 per TP edge, so even a perfect restoration nets at most ~+0.0003-0.0005 locally.
evidence.source: own arithmetic from the counts above; metric node multiplier (linear in N_pred)

evidence.claim: Divisions near the ends are rare: GT parents at t <= 2: 3; at t >= 96: 2 (of 151). The division term cannot rescue the idea.
A global ILP appearance/disappearance sweep (exp13) was already run and kept d2/a0. A time-dependent (clip-end-only) exemption has not been tested.

implementation_notes: CORRECTED MECHANISM: the edge effect comes from the ILP cost set (appearance 0, disappearance 2, edge -p) applied without the standard first/last-frame exemption, not from detector padding (none exists). Part (a) of the hypothesis, the reflection padding and the boundary-only 0.90 threshold on a padding premise, should be dropped. The detector sees frame 99 exactly as it sees frame 50. ILP END FIX, as ultrack does it: in the notebook's ILPSolver call (predict_unet_transformer.py ~L561), replace disappearance_weight=cfg.ilp_disappearance_weight with a polars expression. tracksdata ExprInput accepts pl.Expr: disappearance_weight = pl.when(pl.col('t') == T_LAST).then(C_END).otherwise(2.0), with T_LAST = the max node t of the video (99). START FIX for the asymmetric a0/d2 cost: appearance_weight = pl.when(pl.col('t') == 0).then(-B_START).otherwise(0.0), with 0 < B_START < 2 so an isolated t=0 node (cost 2 - B) is still rejected. The principled values are C_END = 0 and B_START = 1 (half of the per-track cost counts as appearance). Grid C_END {0, 0.5, 1.0} and B_START {0, 0.5, 1.0}. PITFALLS: (1) C_END = 0 makes an isolated t=99 node cost-neutral (objective tie); use C_END >= 0.05 or rely on the tail removing 1-node components. (2) Check that Attr(pl.Expr) resolves its column list in the Kaggle tracksdata version. If not, precompute a node attribute column (e.g. 'dis_w') on the graph and pass the string 'dis_w'. (3) The motion relink REPLACES the ILP edges, so the ILP change matters only through which NODES it selects; restored boundary nodes get re-linked by relink / gap closing like mid-clip nodes. (4) Restored segments at the end are < 6 nodes, and the short-track filter (OUTPUT_MIN_TRACK_LEN 6) removes them unless relink joins them to long tracks. So the ILP fix may need tail change (b), and (b) alone is about break-even. (5) Friend A's raw/ cache holds only the ILP solution (solution = 1 on every node), so no ILP variant can be replayed on CPU without a pre-ILP candidate-graph dump. TAIL CHANGE (b), concrete: in filter_short_track_components, per component compute t0 = min t and t1 = max t over members (nodes_by_id[n]['t']). Use min_len = OUTPUT_MIN_TRACK_LEN, lowered to K_START if t0 == 0 or K_END if t1 == T_LAST, and keep the division/rescue logic unchanged. Measured reach vs cost says this nets ~0.
refined_change: Part (a), detector padding: drop it; the premise is false. The measured clip-edge excess comes from the ILP (tracksdata ILPSolver with appearance 0 / disappearance 2 and no last-frame exemption), which selects no track that starts in the last 3 frames and no track that ends in the first 3. If anything is shipped, it is an ultrack-style time-dependent ILP cost: disappearance C_END (0.05-0.5) at t = T-1 instead of 2, and an appearance bonus -B_START (0.5-1.0) at t = 0. Pair it with a tail rule that keeps components touching t=0 or t=T-1 at >= K (4-5) nodes. Expected value is about zero because the restored nodes are low-value (~0.009 TP edges per node vs 0.061 on average) and the node multiplier cancels most of the edge gain. Recommendation: DEPRIORITISE. Run it only as a free CPU add-on if a pre-ILP candidate-graph dump is made for another ILP idea.
refined_lab_test: Step 1 (replay lab now, CPU, cheap): tail-only grid on SELECTION (64 6bba videos): K_START in {4, 5, off} x K_END in {4, 5, off} in filter_short_track_components. Pre-registered expectation is -0.0003 to +0.0003; success needs >= +0.001 with boundary-frame FN (slots s0-s2, e0-e2) down >= 25% and node count +<= 0.4%. Run CONFIRMATION only if SELECTION passes. Predicted outcome: FAIL, so it can be skipped. Step 2 (ILP end fix) needs a GPU run: one Kaggle 2xT4 pass of the exp39 notebook on the 64 SELECTION train videos, patched to dump the pre-ILP candidate graph per video (all nodes with peak_prob, all candidate edges with edge_prob, as geff) next to the normal raw/ output. Guess: ~0.5-1 GPU h. Then on a CPU kernel, re-solve the ILP with tracksdata. CONTROL first: default weights must reproduce friend A's raw/ solution node-for-node. Then run C_END {0.05, 0.5, 1.0} x B_START {0, 0.5, 1.0}, each with and without the Step-1 tail rule, through the replay from the raw stage. Gate as usual (+0.002, each embryo >= +0.001, 55% win rate). Diagnostic: the raw start fraction at t97-99 and the end fraction at t0-2 should rise from 0 to ~5%, and a_never at s0/e0 should fall toward the 13.9 per 1000 mid rate. Only worth the GPU time if the same candidate-graph dump also serves other ILP experiments.
expected_gain: Local oracle ceiling (all ~154 excess boundary FN recovered, no FP, no node cost) is +0.0011. Tail-only rule (b): about 0 (-0.0003 to +0.0003). ILP clip-end exemption + tail rule: 0 to +0.0005 local, public likely 0 to +0.0003. Well below the +0.002 gate and the 0.97 target, so low priority.
